global_rules: Every quantum-computing benchmark must declare and execute a strong classical baseline before any advantage claim.
Simulator-only results may be labeled quantum_simulated but never quantum_executed or quantum_validated.
Real-QPU records must retain provider, backend, calibration/properties when exposed, program digest, transpiler/compiler identity, shots, raw-result digest, and postprocessing version.
Fault-tolerant candidates must include a resource estimate before being proposed as operationally practical.
No Worldshepherd project may use the word quantum to upgrade the evidence maturity of unrelated physical claims.

benchmarks.problem: Reduced electronic-structure benchmark derived from a physically specified Al-Ti-Mg-Sc-Zr local chemistry or phase motif.
benchmarks.quantum_candidate: VQE or quantum subspace method on a reduced active-space Hamiltonian
classical_baselines: exact diagonalization or selected-CI where reduced problem size permits
DFT or higher-level classical electronic-structure calculation for the associated physical structure
benchmarks.promotion_gate: Quantum result must match a declared reference tolerance and add validated predictive or computational value; it never replaces coupon manufacture or materials characterization.

benchmarks.problem: Discrete reduced-order tile-state optimization for a bounded metasurface objective after the EM physics model is calibrated.
benchmarks.quantum_candidate: QAOA or another explicitly defined combinatorial quantum solver
classical_baselines: MILP or CP-SAT where formulation permits
strong heuristic or local-search baseline for larger instances
benchmarks.promotion_gate: Quantum optimization is retained only when it beats or materially complements the strongest available classical method on the same reduced-order problem. Full-wave Maxwell/FEM/FDTD validation remains authoritative for field behavior.

benchmarks.problem: Constrained routing, assignment, or scheduling instance with a frozen objective and constraint set.
benchmarks.quantum_candidate: Hybrid QAOA or another governed quantum combinatorial solver
classical_baselines: best-known feasible incumbent under the same time budget
benchmarks.promotion_gate: No operational deployment unless quantum/hybrid execution produces a repeatable mission-relevant advantage over classical planning after queueing and communication overhead are included.

benchmarks.problem: Partner-integrated quantum timing, inertial, magnetic, or related PNT sensing under controlled truth-reference conditions.
benchmarks.quantum_candidate: Calibrated external quantum sensor integrated through SARA
classical_baselines: GNSS/INS or laboratory reference appropriate to the modality
conventional sensor of comparable size/power/environment class when available
benchmarks.promotion_gate: Requires calibrated hardware, truth-reference data, uncertainty accounting, and retained sensor provenance. Architecture alone cannot satisfy this gate.

benchmarks.problem: Use quantum electronic-structure methods or quantum-grade sensing to improve material-property estimates or field/force metrology.
benchmarks.quantum_candidate: Reduced electronic-structure calculation and/or calibrated external quantum sensor
benchmarks.promotion_gate: Quantum calculation or sensing may improve materials/metrology evidence but cannot by itself establish anomalous thrust, reactionless propulsion, or net-energy claims.

benchmarks.problem: Determine whether a numerical/permutation inquiry admits a legitimate oracle, Hamiltonian, sampling, search, or optimization formulation with a measurable target.
benchmarks.quantum_candidate: None until a formal problem mapping exists
benchmarks.promotion_gate: Numerical coincidence, permutation structure, prime indexing, or symbolic quantum language is not quantum evidence. A formal computational mapping is mandatory before QPU execution is justified.
